svg.desc: Swimlane chart of non-kinetic counterspace operations by category. Bars are sustained campaigns; points are discrete events; arrowheads mark ongoing campaigns. Solid fill means official or multi-government attribution, outline means researcher or open-source attribution, dashed outline means alleged.

text.tspan: Non-kinetic effects are reversible, deniable, and used
repeatedly in real conflicts. The rules that govern them
are soft law (expert manuals) or carry military
exemptions (ITU Constitution Art. 48). See legal band.

g.aria-label: Iran (jamming from Cuba; later Bulgaria, Libya): Telstar 12 Persian-language broadcasts. 2003 to 2006. Attribution: Alleged (unconfirmed).
Iran: Eutelsat satellites carrying BBC Persian and Voice of America. 2009 to 2012. Attribution: Multiple governments / intergovernmental body.
Russia: Starlink user terminals in Ukraine. 2022 to ongoing. Attribution: Alleged (unconfirmed).
g.text: Russia: Starlink user terminals in Ukr

g.aria-label: Russia (origin locations cited by ITU RRB): Swedish and French broadcasting satellites. 2024 to ongoing. Attribution: Official (single government).
Iraq: GPS receivers of coalition munitions and aircraft. 2003 to 2003. Attribution: Official (single government).
g.text: Iraq: GPS receivers of coalition mun

g.aria-label: North Korea: GPS receivers of aircraft, ships and vehicles in South Korea. 2010 to ongoing. Attribution: Official (single government).

g.aria-label: Russia: GNSS receivers in Ukraine, Crimea and the Black Sea. 2014 to ongoing. Attribution: Researcher / open-source analysis.
g.text: Russia: GNSS receivers in Ukraine, Cri

g.aria-label: Russia: GNSS receivers in and around Syria and the eastern Mediterranean. 2016 to ongoing. Attribution: Researcher / open-source analysis.
g.text: Russia: GNSS receivers in and around S

g.aria-label: Russia: GPS receivers in northern Norway and Finland during NATO Trident Juncture. 2018 to 2018. Attribution: Official (single government).

g.aria-label: Israel and others (multiple actors): GNSS receivers of aircraft over Israel and neighboring states. 2023 to ongoing. Attribution: Official (single government).

g.aria-label: Russia: GNSS receivers of civil aircraft and ships over the Baltic region. 2023 to ongoing. Attribution: Multiple governments / intergovernmental body. Opens 3D scene.

g.aria-label: United States: MSTI-3 (retired USAF experimental satellite). Oct 17, 1997. Attribution: Official (single government). Opens 3D scene.
China: US optical imaging satellites. Jan 1, 2006. Attribution: Alleged (unconfirmed).
Russia: Satellites overflying Russian mobile ICBM units (stated purpose). Mar 1, 2018. Attribution: Official (single government). Opens 3D scene.
Russia: Viasat KA-SAT user terminals (modems) and management network. Feb 24, 2022. Attribution: Multiple governments / intergovernmental body. Opens 3D scene.
